question: Who among the following was arrested and imprisoned for refusing to give evidence against Aurobindo Ghosh in the Bande Mataram conspiracy case?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bipin Chandra Pal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bipin Chandra Pal** was a prominent freedom fighter and one of the leaders of the Indian National Movement.
 
• He was associated with the **Bande Mataram newspaper**, which played a critical role in the Swadeshi movement.
 
• Pal refused to testify against **Aurobindo Ghosh** during the Bande Mataram conspiracy trial in 1907, displaying his unwavering commitment to the nationalist cause.
 
• His refusal to testify led to his arrest and imprisonment, making him a symbol of resistance against colonial oppression.
 
• Pal was one of the **Lal-Bal-Pal trio**, consisting of Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal, who were key figures in advocating aggressive nationalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bande Mataram newspaper:**

 
 
• An English-language newspaper started by Aurobindo Ghosh in 1905 during the Swadeshi Movement.
 
• It was known for its fierce criticism of British colonial rule and advocacy of Indian independence.
 
• It played a vital role in spreading nationalist ideas during the freedom struggle.
 
 
 
• **Aurobindo Ghosh:**
 
 
• Aurobindo Ghosh was a prominent nationalist leader, philosopher, and spiritual thinker in the Indian independence movement.
 
• He actively participated in the Swadeshi movement and was one of the leading figures in the Bengal partition protests.
 
• Later in his life, he became a spiritual guru and founded the Aurobindo Ashram in Pondicherry.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• Launched in 1905 as a response to the partition of Bengal by the British.
 
• The movement emphasized the boycott of British goods and the promotion of Indian-made products.
 
• It marked a significant phase in India’s struggle for independence.
 
 
 
• **Lal-Bal-Pal:**
 
 
• A trio of prominent leaders: Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and Bipin Chandra Pal.
 
• They were known for their radical approach toward achieving independence.
 
• Their efforts significantly influenced the Indian freedom struggle and inspired the youth to actively participate in the movement.
